title: Combine Two Tables
description:
Table `Person` holds people and table `Address` holds their addresses.

Write a query to report the `firstName`, `lastName`, `city` and `state` of every person. **If a person has no address recorded, still report them**, with `NULL` for `city` and `state`.

Return the result in any order.
hint: A plain INNER JOIN would drop people with no address. Which join keeps every row from the left table?
outputExplanation: Each row of the result corresponds to one (person, address) pair. People without a matching address still appear once, with city and state set to NULL. People with multiple addresses appear once per address (fan-out).

tests.name: Example
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO Person VALUES (1,'Wang','Allen'),(2,'Alice','Bob'),(3,'Deo','Vedant');
INSERT INTO Address VALUES (1,2,'New York City','New York'),(2,3,'Leetcode','California');
